newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares close mixed, foreign funds buyers.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares close mixed, foreign funds buyers.

text.p: Bombay share prices finished mixed on Tuesday in range-bound trade with selective foreign institutional buying, brokers said.
They said the market attracted resistance at higher levels and turned back towards the close.
The brokers said foreign funds bought Otis, Swaraj Engines, Ranbaxy, ITC, MTNL, TELCO, Bajaj Auto, BPCL, HPCL, ICICI and NALCO.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 3.00 points, or 0.09 percent, higher at a provisional 3,334.09.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index slipped 1.34 points, or 0.14 percent, lower at a provisional 967.66.
The 500-share CRISIL index shed 1.54 points to a provisional 650.09.
Traders said they expect activity to remain sluggish due to slowing economy, shrinking company profit growth and uncertain political prospects.

A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities houses projected an average 20.6 percent rise in the net profit of 30 index firms during the first half ending September 30, 1996 from around 40 percent a year ago.
Net sales growth was pegged at a modest 16.5 percent.
Analysts said declining global prices of commodities like petrochemicals, aluminium and steel coupled with cuts in import duties of these products would hit several index firms.
Bajaj Auto rose 15.50 rupees to 990.75, ITC 4.25 to 298.25, M&M 2.25 to 330.50, Reliance 2.0 to 197, TISCO 1.75 to 173.50, Ranbaxy 2.75 to 609.75 and ACC 18.0 to 1,869.25.
Gujarat Ambuja Cement shed 3.0 rupees to 290, BSES 1.25 to 178.75, TELCO 5.0 to 457.50 and Tata Power 2.0 to 137.50.
